items.title: the frozen request repeats recovery instructions naming guarded commands, with no relay framing

prompt: Work item: uaa-0070 — frame or reattribute the recovery notes at their source, so no rendered surface hands a relay-hosted agent an imperative naming a guarded command.

`crates/xtask/src/agent_maintenance/contract_policy.rs:181-184` authors two `execution_contract.recovery.notes`. Note 2 is an imperative: "fix the Codex binary/auth state and rerun `execute-agent-maintenance --dry-run` before write mode".

uaa-0068 framed the rendered docs: `docs.rs` prefixes the HANDOFF `## Recovery` section with a sentence covering every command it names, its notes included. That framing does not reach `governance/maintenance-request.toml`, which repeats both notes as frozen data and which the packet prompt orders the agent to read first.

Two controls already cover that surface: the packet prompt prohibits invoking the relay family unconditionally, and the environment guard refuses the command. This row closes the remaining contradiction between two documents the agent reads, which is the defect class uaa-0068 was about.

The fix is to reattribute the note text to the actor outside the relay, at its source, which reaches every surface including the TOML. Blast radius, measured 2026-09-25: about sixteen pinned strings across eight test files (`c4_spec_ci_wiring.rs`, `agent_maintenance_prepare.rs`, `agent_maintenance_execute.rs`, and four harnesses) plus `.github/workflows/agent-maintenance-open-pr.yml`, because `c4_spec_ci_wiring.rs:84` binds the workflow's copy of the sentence to the contract's.
`docs/specs/maintenance-request-contract-v1.md:426` is permissive about this field's content, so the text is not spec-pinned; the workflow coupling is what makes the change wide.

notes: Raised 2026-09-25 during uaa-0068's second remediation review, and deferred by the lead the same day: the change would touch the nightly's own workflow days before the first closeout rehearsal, for a surface two other controls already cover.

The regression test added with uaa-0068 (`crates/xtask/tests/agent_maintenance_prepare.rs`) enforces the set of rendered docs that name guarded tooling, but checks the framing only at document level, so it would not catch a single section that frames one command and orders another. Section-level proof needs a heading parser and a per-doc exception table; fold that into this row rather than adding it separately.

items.title: xtask test targets exec the shared debug/xtask binary while cargo relinks it, so execs wedge or no-op

prompt: Work item: uaa-0071 — stop xtask test targets from racing cargo over the one `debug/xtask` binary they all exec.

Roughly twenty test files spawn `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask")` as a subprocess. `cargo test` builds and relinks that single bin target while already-built test binaries are running, so a concurrent exec can observe it mid-write.

Two independent measurements on 2026-09-25, from different processes, describe one mechanism. First: a `cargo test -p xtask` run hung for 1h12m inside `refresh_publication_entrypoint`, whose five live children (three `support-matrix --check`, two `capability-matrix --check`) were each sampled entirely in `_dyld_start` — blocked in the dynamic loader, never reaching `main`. Second: a review lane running the suite from a non-git extract with a cold target dir got 28 failures whose common shape was `debug/xtask` exiting 0 with empty stderr, i.e. a binary that loaded but did nothing.
The same lane proved the failures are unrelated to the relay marker: with `XTASK_AGENT_MAINTENANCE_RUN_ID` set and unset, the sorted failing-test name sets were identical.

This has been misread three times in one day as a pre-existing load-sensitive flake, because every affected test passes when its target runs alone. `uaa-0057` and `uaa-0067` were both filed under that reading and should be re-examined against this mechanism before being chased separately.
Candidate directions, none chosen: give the spawning tests their own copy of the binary; serialize the targets that exec it; or have them resolve a binary built once, outside the test run.

notes: Raised 2026-09-25 while auditing a hung background process from a review lane. Not a product defect; it makes `make preflight` and full-suite runs unreliable, which is what has made preflight evidence hard to trust in this work.
Deliberately not the deletion hazard the same lane reported: that scratch checkout was removed by the lead's own cleanup `rm -rf` while the lane was still live, not by any test.

Codex verification on 2026-09-25 demonstrated a more specific mechanism for the empty-success symptom: refresh_publication_entrypoint writes a fixture xtask with fn main() {} and invokes nested cargo commands. An inherited absolute CARGO_TARGET_DIR makes that fixture replace the real shared debug/xtask binary. In one isolated probe its size changed from 38,795,664 to 404,352 bytes and --help changed from 4,673 output bytes to zero, both exit 0. Running without the override keeps each fixture target separate; the complete xtask suite then passed. The earlier claim that outer cargo relinks while running tests is not established by those symptoms alone, and the historical dyld hang has not been independently attributed. Use a worktree-local default target directory for verification; any harness-level isolation change remains separate work.
